notes.summary: Classification means finding the odd one out: three options follow one common rule and one does not. Expect 2–3 questions in Tier 1 with words, numbers or letter groups.

concepts.title: Find the common rule
concepts.body: Look for what three items share: same category (fruits, planets), same property (prime, perfect square), or same letter gap. The item that breaks the rule is the answer.

concepts.title: Number properties to test
concepts.body: Prime / composite, even / odd, perfect square / cube, divisible by a number, sum of digits, n² + 1 type pairs.

concepts.title: Letter groups
concepts.body: Write positions (A=1 … Z=26) and check the gap between letters. Example: BDF has gaps +2, +2.

varieties.name: Odd word out
varieties.how: Name the group for each word; the one that does not fit is odd.

varieties.name: Odd number / pair out
varieties.how: Test prime, square, cube and simple rules like n² + 1.

varieties.name: Odd letter group out
varieties.how: Write positions and compare the gaps.

tips: Try the simplest rule first (category, prime, square) before complex ones.
If two rules seem to work, pick the one that leaves exactly one item out.
traps: Do not pick an item just because it "looks" different; there must be a clear rule.

questions.q: Select the odd word from the given alternatives.
questions.solution:
Rose, Lotus and Lily are flowers.
Mango is a fruit, so it is the odd one.

questions.q: Select the odd number from the given alternatives.
questions.solution:
13, 17 and 29 are prime numbers.
21 = 3 × 7 is not prime.
So 21 is the odd one.

B D F: +2, +2. H J L: +2, +2. M O Q: +2, +2.
R T W: R+2 = T, but T+3 = W.
So RTW is odd.

27 = 3³, 64 = 4³, 125 = 5³: all perfect cubes.
144 = 12² is a perfect square, not a cube.
So 144 is odd.

questions.q: Select the number-pair in which the two numbers are NOT related in the same way as in the other pairs.

questions.solution:
Tiger, Leopard and Lion belong to the cat family.
Wolf belongs to the dog family.
So Wolf is odd.

flashcards.back: Find the rule shared by three; the one that breaks it is the answer.
